issues.legal_issue: A pending application by one judgment debtor to set aside an execution sale does not bar other judgment debtors from seeking to set aside the sale by making the required deposit.
material_facts: A house was sold in execution of a money decree against several judgment debtors.
One judgment debtor applied to set aside the sale on grounds relating to the sale procedure.
Other judgment debtors later applied to set aside the sale by depositing the decretal amount and the purchaser’s compensation.
issues.conclusion: The application by one judgment debtor did not bar the other judgment debtors’ application, and the sale was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21, Rules 89 and 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an application by one judgment debtor under Rule 90 does not prevent other judgment debtors from applying under Rule 89 when they make the deposit required by that rule. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: execution_sale_proceeding and one_judgment_debtor_challenges_sale and different_judgment_debtors_seek_sale_relief and required_amount_deposited

predicates.execution_sale_proceeding: Immovable property was sold in execution of a decree.
predicates.one_judgment_debtor_challenges_sale: One judgment debtor applied to have the execution sale set aside.
predicates.different_judgment_debtors_seek_sale_rel: Judgment debtors other than the applicant in the challenge applied for relief from the sale.
predicates.required_amount_deposited: The judgment debtors seeking relief deposited the amounts required for that relief.

issues.definition: When property is sold in execution, one judgment debtor’s challenge to the sale does not bar different judgment debtors from seeking relief if they deposit the required amounts.

issues.legal_issue: An application seeking to deposit the required sums to undo an execution sale may qualify as an application to set aside the sale even without an express prayer for that relief.
material_facts: The application identified the auction sale and stated that the applicant wanted to deposit the amounts associated with the sale.
The application did not expressly ask the court to set aside the sale.
The application was described as being under Order 21, Rule 89, and its purpose was apparent from its contents.
issues.conclusion: The application was properly read as an application to set aside the sale.
issues.legal_principle: For an application under Order 21, Rule 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court may consider the application’s substance and evident purpose; an express prayer to set aside the sale is not necessary where the application clearly seeks to make the required deposit for that purpose. The court distinguished the cited decisions and did not rely on them.

rule.if: execution_sale_proceeding and application_identifies_sale and application_seeks_required_deposit and no_express_set_aside_prayer

predicates.execution_sale_proceeding: Immovable property was sold in execution of a decree.
predicates.application_identifies_sale: The application identified the property’s auction sale.
predicates.application_seeks_required_deposit: The applicant stated an intention to deposit the sums required to obtain relief from the sale.
predicates.no_express_set_aside_prayer: The application did not expressly ask the court to set aside the sale.

issues.definition: An application concerning an execution sale is treated as seeking to set aside the sale when it identifies the sale and seeks the required deposit for that purpose, even if it contains no express prayer for that relief.

issues.legal_issue: A proper deposit made by a judgment debtor on behalf of other judgment debtors may benefit those other judgment debtors and support setting aside the execution sale.
material_facts: The application for relief was made on behalf of several judgment debtors.
The full amount required for relief was deposited on their behalf.
One of the judgment debtors had a separate pending application challenging the sale.
issues.conclusion: The proper deposit benefited the other judgment debtors, and their application was effective to set aside the sale despite the separate pending challenge.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21, Rule 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure, when a judgment debtor makes the required deposit on behalf of the judgment debtors seeking relief, the benefit of a proper deposit may accrue to those other judgment debtors. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: execution_sale_proceeding and application_made_for_multiple_judgment_debtors and deposit_made_on_their_behalf and required_amount_deposited

predicates.execution_sale_proceeding: Immovable property was sold in execution of a decree.
predicates.application_made_for_multiple_judgment_d: An application for relief from the sale was made for more than one judgment debtor.
predicates.deposit_made_on_their_behalf: A judgment debtor deposited money on behalf of the judgment debtors seeking relief.
predicates.required_amount_deposited: The full amount required for relief was deposited.

issues.definition: In an execution-sale proceeding, a proper deposit made on behalf of multiple judgment debtors may benefit each of them when their application seeks relief from the sale.

issues.legal_issue: When an execution sale is set aside, the court may direct repayment of the auction purchaser’s purchase money and account for interest earned or not earned while the money was held.
material_facts: The auction purchaser’s money had remained in court after the sale.
The money was later invested in a fixed deposit and earned interest.
The court directed repayment of the purchase money and the interest earned, and required the judgment debtors to pay interest for the period when the money earned none.
issues.conclusion: The auction purchaser could withdraw the purchase money together with the interest earned, while the judgment debtors were directed to pay interest for the period when the money was not earning interest.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21, Rule 93 of the Code of Civil Procedure entitles the court to direct repayment of purchase money when a sale is set aside. The court also addressed the interest consequences according to whether the money held in court was earning interest.

predicates.execution_sale_set_aside: The court set aside an execution sale.
predicates.purchaser_money_held_by_court: The auction purchaser’s money remained with the court after the sale.
predicates.interest_accrued_or_was_not_accruing: The money held by the court earned interest during some period or did not earn interest during some period.

issues.definition: When an execution sale is set aside and the purchaser’s money has been held by the court, repayment accounts for interest earned and for any period when the money earned none.
